Finite-dimensional linear algebra and sp.id: Finite-dimensional linear algebra and spectral theory
Finite-dimensional linear algebra and sp.description: Mathlib foundations for matrices, positive definiteness, inner products, eigenspaces, and singular values.
provisional_members: Positive semidefinite and positive definite matrices
Finite-dimensional linear algebra and sp.mathlib_notes: Verified in the pinned checkout. Matrix positivity is defined in Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/PosDef.lean, the symmetric spectral basis in Mathlib/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/Spectrum.lean, singular values in Mathlib/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/SingularValues.lean, and orthogonal projection in Mathlib/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/Projection/Basic.lean. The singular-value API exposes Gram-spectrum values rather than a complete singular-vector decomposition. The generic projection declaration requires HasOrthogonalProjection; finite-dimensional completeness supplies the intended specialization.

Differential and integral calculus.description: Mathlib foundations for Frechet derivatives, higher derivatives, Taylor estimates, and Bochner and interval integration.
Differential and integral calculus.mathlib_notes: Verified in the pinned checkout. HasFDerivAt and fderiv are defined in Mathlib/Analysis/Calculus/FDeriv/Defs.lean; gradients are in Analysis/Calculus/Gradient/Basic.lean. No standalone Hessian declaration was found, so the fine graph must use iteratedFDeriv at order two or introduce a proved bridge. HasFTaylorSeriesUpTo records derivative jets and is not itself a Taylor formula; actual expansions and bounds include taylor_isLittleO and taylor_mean_remainder_bound in Analysis/Calculus/Taylor.lean and map_add_eq_sum_add_integral_iteratedFDeriv in TaylorIntegral.lean. Bochner integration is under MeasureTheory/Integral/Bochner, and the interval fundamental theorem is in MeasureTheory/Integral/IntervalIntegral/FundThmCalculus.lean.

Measure-theoretic probability and condit.description: Mathlib foundations for probability measures, laws, independent random variables, integration, conditional expectation, and integral expectation inequalities.
Measure-theoretic probability and condit.mathlib_notes: Verified in the pinned checkout. Laws and finite product laws are in Mathlib/Probability/HasLaw.lean, independence and infinite products under Mathlib/Probability/Independence, and an explicit iid realization in Mathlib/Probability/HasLawExists.lean. Conditional expectation is under MeasureTheory/Function/ConditionalExpectation, the Radon-Nikodym derivative under MeasureTheory/Measure/Decomposition/Lebesgue, and Bochner integration under MeasureTheory/Integral/Bochner. Integral Jensen and its finite-measure average variant are in Mathlib/Analysis/Convex/Integral.lean; the probability-measure theorem retains closed-domain, continuity, almost-everywhere membership, and Bochner integrability hypotheses. Fine statements must retain the integrability and sigma-algebra hypotheses of condExp and the ENNReal-valued almost-everywhere semantics of rnDeriv.

Convex analysis and normed-space geometr.description: Mathlib foundations for convex functions and sets, strong convexity, finite Jensen inequalities, norms, duality, and Hilbert-space geometry.
provisional_members: Finite convex combinations and finite Jensen inequality
Hilbert spaces and continuous linear maps
Convex analysis and normed-space geometr.mathlib_notes: Verified in the pinned checkout. Strong convexity and finite Jensen results are in adjacent Mathlib/Analysis/Convex files; StrongDual is in Mathlib/Topology/Algebra/Module/ContinuousLinearMap/Basic.lean; ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_le_bound is defined in Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Operator/Basic.lean; and the Hilbert-space Riesz map innerSL is in Mathlib/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/LinearMap.lean. Integral Jensen is assigned to the probability-and-expectation foundation because its statement depends on both a probability measure and Bochner integration. Mathlib's strong-convexity file does not supply the derivative characterizations needed downstream, which remain project-local assembly or proofs.

Matrix algebra and Gaussian conditioning.description: Closed-form quadratic optimization, block-matrix inversion, and Gaussian conditioning through Schur complements.
depends_on: Finite-dimensional linear algebra and spectral theory
Matrix algebra and Gaussian conditioning.mathlib_notes: Pinned Mathlib exactly covers scalar Young inequalities, operational Schur complements, both block inverse formulas, Woodbury, the identity-plus-BB-transpose inverse by specialization, Schur determinant factorizations, multivariate Gaussian means/covariance, and coordinate-block marginals. Quadratic minimization, completed-square and Fenchel-Young forms require assembly. The semidefinite range/unboundedness criterion, push-through and all-ones specializations, explicit two-by-two inverse theorem, Gaussian density factorization, and conditional Gaussian mean/covariance theorem are absent. Supporting files include Matrix/Invertible.lean, NonsingularInverse.lean, PosDef.lean, Adjugate.lean, Determinant/Basic.lean, and Probability/Distributions/Gaussian/Multivariate.lean.

Spectral and differential matrix tools.description: Spectral decompositions and the matrix derivatives used throughout the estimators.
depends_on: Finite-dimensional linear algebra and spectral theory
Spectral and differential matrix tools.mathlib_notes: At pinned Mathlib commit 905b95818eb32af7874a58b427f50c1711a5e96c, the real-symmetric spectral decomposition is covered through the Hermitian spectral theorem and Matrix.isHermitian_iff_isSymm; the positive-semidefinite eigenvalue criterion and sigmoid definition/derivative are also direct. LinearMap.sq_singularValues_fin and LinearMap.hasEigenvalue_adjoint_comp_self_sq_singularValues identify squared singular values with the spectrum of the domain Gram operator T* T, while the rectangular charpoly multiplication lemmas relate the two Gram spectra; completing the codomain Gram statement still requires assembly. No economy-SVD factorization or singular-vector API was found, leaving the economy SVD, singular-vector equations, Gram eigenvectors (Exercise 1.5), symmetric dilation spectrum, and dilation eigenvectors (Exercise 1.6) uncovered. Inner-product and squared-norm Frechet derivative lemmas support assembly of the quadratic and least-squares gradients, but no dedicated gradient formulas or Hessian theorems were found. Sigmoid differentiation is present, but the logistic gradient and Hessian (Exercise 1.7) are uncovered. Ring-inverse differentiation, trace linearity, and the polynomial derivative of det(I + tM) at zero provide ingredients for Exercise 1.8, but no exact inverse-trace or log-determinant matrix-gradient theorem was found. Supporting files are Mathlib/Analysis/Matrix/PosDef.lean, Mathlib/Analysis/Matrix/Order.lean, Mathlib/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/SingularValues.lean, Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/Charpoly/Basic.lean, Mathlib/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/Calculus.lean, Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Sigmoid.lean, Mathlib/Analysis/Calculus/FDeriv/Mul.lean, Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/Trace.lean, and Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/Charpoly/Coeff.lean.

Elementary probability and convexity bou.description: Moment identities and basic devices underlying all later concentration arguments.
provisional_members: Variance of an independent sample mean
Jensen inequality on the real line
Elementary probability and convexity bou.mathlib_notes: Pinned Mathlib directly covers Markov, Chebyshev, the sample-mean CLT, a stronger Lp law of large numbers, countable union bounds, generic Chernoff, tail integration, and vector-valued Jensen under explicit hypotheses. Variance scaling, independent-sum variance, and identical-distribution invariance assemble the exact sigma^2/n sample-mean variance; combining this with Chebyshev gives the book's finite convergence-in-probability estimate. The supremum-tail result is a countable-union corollary with nonempty/boundedness conditions, not a dedicated theorem.

Hoeffding and sub-Gaussian concentration.description: Bounded-variable, martingale, Laplace-transform, tail, sum, and moment formulations of sub-Gaussian concentration.
Hoeffding and sub-Gaussian concentration.mathlib_notes: Pinned revision 905b958 provides the MGF predicate, Hoeffding's bounded-variable Laplace lemma, centered bounded-variable sub-Gaussianity, one-sided tails for independent and conditionally sub-Gaussian sums, scaling, negation, and Gaussian MGF identities. The book's bounded-average and two-sided confidence forms require rescaling and union-bound assembly. No exact Gaussian tail sandwich, quantitative even-moment/converse package, negative-Laplace inequality, or conditional bounded-difference Hoeffding lemma was found. Mathlib parameter c corresponds to the book's tau^2.

Bounded differences and Bernstein concen.description: Function-level bounded differences and variance-sensitive scalar concentration.
Bounded differences and Bernstein concen.mathlib_notes: Pinned Mathlib provides Hamming/Lipschitz interfaces, natural filtrations, conditional expectations and martingales, conditional sub-Gaussian predicates, sum composition, and generic Chernoff-MGF bounds. It lacks a coordinatewise bounded-variation API, McDiarmid's inequality, the tailored Doob decomposition and increment bound, a bounded conditional Hoeffding lemma, vector Hoeffding, and centered or noncentered Bernstein/Bennett/subexponential concentration. Supporting files include InformationTheory/Hamming.lean, Probability/Martingale/Basic.lean, Probability/Process/Filtration.lean, and Probability/Moments/Basic.lean.

Maxima and smooth-sum expectation bounds.description: Logarithmic maxima bounds and expectation control for smooth convex functions of independent sums.
provisional_members: Weighted simultaneous confidence and penalized-selection bound (Exercise 1.24)
Maxima and smooth-sum expectation bounds.mathlib_notes: Pinned revision 905b958 provides centered sub-Gaussian MGF, CGF, and one-sided tail APIs; finite/countable set union bounds; the layer-cake tail-integral formula; Gaussian measures and MGFs; convexity, C1 calculus, and a chordal strong-concavity/semiconcavity surrogate; and independence plus bilinear-expectation factorization for partial sums. MeasureTheory.measure_iUnion_fintype_le covers the maximum tail union bound after rewriting the maximum event as a finite union. Uncovered as dedicated statements are: Expected sub-Gaussian maximum; Expected absolute maximum (Exercise 1.22); Gaussian maximum lower bound (Exercise 1.23); Weighted simultaneous confidence and penalized-selection bound (Exercise 1.24); Norm-relative smoothness definition; and Smooth convex independent-sum bound (Exercise 1.25). These require assembly or new theorems. StrongConcaveOn with negative modulus is related to the book's upper quadratic smoothness condition, but Mathlib/Analysis/Convex/Strong.lean explicitly leaves derivative properties as TODO, so no verified equivalence was found. Material ambiguity: Exercise 1.24 permits zero weights although its Real.log(1 / pi_i) penalty is not the intended extended-real infinity at pi_i = 0; a formal statement should require positive weights or use an extended-real penalty.

Deterministic quadrature error.description: Trapezoidal approximation of expectations under differentiability or periodicity assumptions.
Deterministic quadrature error.mathlib_notes: Pinned Mathlib has a dedicated uniform-grid trapezoidal-rule definition, its signed error, the one-panel endpoint formula, exact decomposition into adjacent-panel errors, and the sharp C2 bound |error| <= |b-a|^3*zeta/(12*N^2). The book's [0,1] estimator and L/(12*n^2) result are direct specializations (Mathlib defines error with the opposite sign, immaterial under absolute value). AffineMap.lineMap_apply_ring gives the explicit affine interpolant formula, but its integral identity still needs assembly from elementary interval integrals. No public theorem was found for the pointwise L*x*(1-x)/2 interpolation error, the O(1/n) first-derivative-only rate, or the O(1/n^s) periodic smooth-function rate.

Matrix and operator concentration.description: Hoeffding and Bernstein inequalities for symmetric matrices, rectangular dilations, and Hilbert-space operators.
depends_on: Finite-dimensional linear algebra and spectral theory
Matrix and operator concentration.mathlib_notes: Pinned-checkout searches for matrix/operator Hoeffding, Bernstein, intrinsic-dimension concentration, Hermitian dilation concentration, and sample covariance bounds found no matching declaration. Positive-semidefinite order, eigenvalues, and operator norms exist in prerequisite clusters, but no member providing matrix concentration itself is in Mathlib. The complete theorem package and its trace-exponential proof machinery must be developed or sourced independently.

provisional_members: Learning algorithm as a dataset-to-predictor map
Supervised learning setup and evaluation.mathlib_notes: Pinned Mathlib supplies independence of indexed random variables, identical distribution through equal pushforward laws, and finite product probability measures, which are enough to state i.i.d. train/test samples. Searches found no unified dataset, learner, training/validation/test split, cross-validation, hyperparameter-selection, or neighboring-learning-paradigm API. Those definitions are project-local; their measurable interfaces must be built explicitly on the probability substrate.

Loss risk and Bayes decision theory.description: Formal performance criteria and pointwise optimal prediction under common losses.
Loss risk and Bayes decision theory.mathlib_notes: Pinned Mathlib has a generic kernel-valued decision-theory API with extended-nonnegative losses, average and Bayes risk, posterior expected loss, measurable argmin estimators, and the theorem that such an estimator is Bayes. The file explicitly leaves general measurable selection as a TODO. No prediction-specific zero-one, square, absolute, pinball, or epsilon-insensitive loss library, empirical/conditional/excess-risk API, or the book's classifier/regression Bayes-characterization theorems were found. Adapting the generic estimator API to supervised prediction and real-valued risks remains project work.

Existence of iid random variables.description: For any index type and any probability measure on an arbitrary measurable space, constructs a measurable mutually independent family on a product probability space, with every coordinate having the specified common law.
depends_on: Independent coordinates on an infinite product space
Existence of iid random variables.mathlib_notes: Verified in the pinned checkout. exists_iid allows an arbitrary, possibly empty or uncountable index type and assumes only a measurable-space structure on the target and IsProbabilityMeasure mu. It returns a source measurable space, a probability measure P, and measurable maps X i with common HasLaw mu and iIndepFun X P. Its implementation uses the full product space, MeasurableSpace.pi, Measure.infinitePi, and coordinate evaluations. No countability, nonemptiness, countable-generation, or standard-Borel hypotheses occur. IdentDistrib is not in the conclusion, although the common HasLaw witnesses imply pairwise IdentDistrib. The product-measure construction is noncomputable and transitively uses Classical.choice.

Radon-Nikodym derivative of measures.description: Defines Mathlib's noncomputable total ENNReal-valued density component of the Lebesgue decomposition of mu relative to nu, with the exact zero function as fallback when no decomposition exists.
Radon-Nikodym derivative of measures.mathlib_notes: Verified in the pinned checkout. For measures mu and nu on the same measurable space, rnDeriv mu nu : alpha -> ENNReal is a noncomputable irreducible total definition. It has no finiteness or decomposition typeclass parameter: it internally tests the proposition HaveLebesgueDecomposition mu nu, classically chooses its measurable density when true, and is exactly the zero function when false. Under HaveLebesgueDecomposition mu nu, haveLebesgueDecomposition_spec gives measurability, mutual singularity of the selected singular part with nu, and mu = mu.singularPart nu + nu.withDensity (mu.rnDeriv nu). The standard instance assumes SFinite mu and SigmaFinite nu. The argument order is the density component of mu relative to reference measure nu; this node does not assert absolute-continuity recovery or almost-everywhere uniqueness.

Measurability of the Radon-Nikodym deriv.description: Establishes measurability of the extended-nonnegative Radon-Nikodym derivative.
Measurability of the Radon-Nikodym deriv.mathlib_notes: The verified theorem is unconditional because the definition is zero when no decomposition instance exists.

Radon-Nikodym representation theorem.description: For measures mu and nu with HaveLebesgueDecomposition mu nu, characterizes mu absolutely continuous with respect to nu by nu.withDensity (mu.rnDeriv nu) = mu.
Radon-Nikodym representation theorem.mathlib_notes: Verified in the pinned checkout. Under HaveLebesgueDecomposition mu nu, the theorem states that mu is absolutely continuous with respect to nu exactly when nu.withDensity (mu.rnDeriv nu) = mu, where mu.rnDeriv nu is ENNReal-valued. The standard instance requires SFinite mu and SigmaFinite nu; two sigma-finite measures are a special case. Although rnDeriv is totalized to zero without a decomposition, this representation theorem is not unconditional.

Almost-everywhere uniqueness of the Rado.id: Almost-everywhere uniqueness of the Radon-Nikodym derivative
Almost-everywhere uniqueness of the Rado.description: Proves that a measurable or almost-everywhere-measurable ENNReal density in a Lebesgue decomposition agrees almost everywhere, under the sigma-finite reference measure, with rnDeriv.
Almost-everywhere uniqueness of the Rado.mathlib_notes: Verified in the pinned checkout. With SigmaFinite nu, a measurable f : alpha -> ENNReal, s mutually singular with nu, and mu = s + nu.withDensity f, eq_rnDeriv proves f = mu.rnDeriv nu almost everywhere with respect to nu. No sigma-finiteness assumption on mu or pre-existing decomposition instance is required. The eq_rnDeriv₀ variant needs only AEMeasurable f nu. Measure-level withDensity uniqueness does not require sigma-finiteness; the function-level result uses withDensity_eq_iff_of_sigmaFinite and measurable_rnDeriv. This is distinct from the absolute-continuity reconstruction theorem.

Conditional expectation.description: Defines Mathlib's noncomputable total pointwise conditional-expectation representative for an arbitrary measure and a real normed-space-valued function, with no completeness assumption in the definition.
Conditional expectation.mathlib_notes: Verified in the pinned checkout. For mu with underlying measurable structure m0, condExp takes an explicit measurable structure m and has type alpha -> E for any real normed-space codomain E; the scoped notation mu[f | m] expands to condExp m mu f. The definition requires neither completeness nor a probability or finite-measure assumption. It is exactly zero when m is not below m0, when SigmaFinite of the trimmed measure fails, or when f is not Bochner integrable. Under valid hypotheses, it returns f if f is strongly measurable with respect to m, and otherwise returns the strongly measurable representative built from condExpL1. Completeness and integral-characterization laws belong to downstream nodes.

Strong measurability of conditional expe.description: Establishes strong measurability of conditional expectation for the conditioning sigma-algebra.
Strong measurability of conditional expe.mathlib_notes: Verified in the pinned checkout. For measurable structures m and m0 on alpha, mu : Measure[m0] alpha, f : alpha -> E, and a real normed-space codomain E, stronglyMeasurable_condExp proves StronglyMeasurable[m] (mu[f | m]). It requires neither m <= m0, trimmed sigma-finiteness, integrability, nor completeness because every invalid branch of the totalized conditional expectation is zero.

Integrability of conditional expectation.description: For any function into a complete real normed space, its totalized conditional expectation is Bochner integrable with respect to the same measure, without hypotheses on input integrability, sigma-algebra inclusion, or trimmed sigma-finiteness.
Integrability of conditional expectation.mathlib_notes: Verified in the pinned checkout. For measurable structures m and m0, a measure mu with underlying structure m0, an arbitrary f : alpha -> E, and a complete real normed-space codomain E, integrable_condExp proves Integrable (mu[f | m]) mu. There is no hypothesis that f is integrable, that m <= m0, or that a trimmed measure is sigma-finite. Failure of any validity condition makes condExp zero; completeness is a theorem assumption rather than a totalization branch.

Conditional expectation set-integral ide.description: Gives the defining integral identity on sets measurable in the conditioning sigma-algebra.
Conditional expectation set-integral ide.mathlib_notes: The verified theorem retains m <= m0, SigmaFinite of the trimmed measure, Integrable f mu, completeness of the codomain, and MeasurableSet[m] s. Both set integrals use mu restricted to s; the theorem is not an invalid-case totalization identity.

Uniqueness of conditional expectation.description: Uniquely identifies conditional expectation up to almost-everywhere equality from conditional almost-everywhere strong measurability, local integrability, and finite-set integral identities.
Uniqueness of conditional expectation.mathlib_notes: Verified in the pinned checkout. Under m <= m0, sigma-finiteness of the trimmed measure, completeness of the real normed codomain, and Integrable f mu, the theorem assumes that g is almost-everywhere strongly measurable with respect to m and integrable on every m-measurable finite-mu-measure set, with the same set integrals as f there. It concludes g = mu[f | m] almost everywhere with respect to mu. The previously guessed ae_eq_condExp_iff_eq_setIntegral declaration does not exist; an iff is derivable using setIntegral_condExp but is not a named theorem.

Law of total expectation.description: Identifies the integral of a conditional expectation with the original integral.
Law of total expectation.mathlib_notes: Verified in the pinned checkout. For an arbitrary measure mu, a complete real normed-space codomain E, m <= m0, and sigma-finiteness of the trimmed measure, integral_condExp states that the integral of mu[f | m] with respect to mu equals the integral of f. It assumes neither Integrable f mu nor a probability or finite-measure structure. The integrable branch specializes setIntegral_condExp to Set.univ; in the nonintegrable branch, both condExp and the Bochner integral are zero by their totalized definitions.

Tower property of conditional expectatio.description: Shows that nested conditioning onto smaller sigma-algebras collapses almost everywhere.
Tower property of conditional expectatio.mathlib_notes: Verified in the pinned checkout. For m1 <= m2 <= m0, an arbitrary measure mu on m0, arbitrary f : alpha -> E, and a complete real normed-space codomain, condExp_condExp_of_le proves that conditioning first on m2 and then on m1 equals direct conditioning on m1 almost everywhere with respect to mu. It assumes only sigma-finiteness of the trim along m2 <= m0; neither input integrability nor sigma-finiteness of the smaller trim is required because conditional expectation is totalized to zero in invalid cases.

Convex sets.description: Convex subsets expressed through closure under nonnegative affine combinations for a semiring with a separate partial order acting on an additive commutative monoid.
Convex sets.mathlib_notes: Verified in the pinned checkout. The minimal assumptions for Convex, the two-point and segment equivalences, and segment closure are Semiring R, PartialOrder R, AddCommMonoid E, and SMul R E, with no module, ordered-semiring compatibility, topology, norm, or real-scalar assumption. Convex is defined through StarConvex; convex_iff_add_mem gives the nonnegative two-point formula, convex_iff_div supplies the normalized division form used by finite centers of mass, and convex_iff_segment_subset gives segment closure. Empty and universal sets use the same weak assumptions, while singleton and subsingleton convexity require Module R E. The distinct Convexity.IsConvexSet API is not substituted because downstream Analysis/Convex declarations use Convex.

Convex functions on a set.description: Convex functions on convex domains, under the weak additive, scalar-action, and partial-order assumptions used by Mathlib.
Convex functions on a set.mathlib_notes: Verified in the pinned checkout. ConvexOn assumes Semiring R, PartialOrder R, AddCommMonoid E, AddCommMonoid B, PartialOrder B, SMul R E, and SMul R B. It bundles Convex R s with the nonnegative two-point inequality. The definition requires no module laws, ordered-semiring compatibility, topology, norm, or completeness. Its only foundation dependency here is Convex sets.

Strong convexity on a set.description: Quadratic strengthening of convexity for real-valued functions on a real normed space, with arbitrary real modulus.
Strong convexity on a set.mathlib_notes: Verified in the pinned checkout. StrongConvexOn is defined for a real normed space and a real-valued function, with no completeness, inner-product, or sign assumption on the real modulus m. It is definitionally UniformConvexOn s (fun r => m / 2 * r^2) f and bundles Convex Real s with the nonnegative two-point inequality whose correction term is a * b * (m / 2) * norm(x - y)^2. The definition does not use ConvexOn directly; ordinary and strict convexity consequences require the usual sign hypotheses.

Strong convexity as shifted convexity.description: Characterizes strong convexity by subtracting the quadratic term m / 2 times the squared norm.
Strong convexity as shifted convexity.mathlib_notes: Verified in the pinned checkout. For a real inner-product space, arbitrary set s, arbitrary real modulus m, and f : E -> Real, strongConvexOn_iff_convex states that StrongConvexOn s m f is equivalent to ConvexOn Real s (fun x => f x - m / 2 * norm x ^ 2). No positivity, separate convex-set, or completeness premise is required.

Finite Jensen inequality.description: Jensen's inequality for a finite convex combination over a strict ordered field and a partially ordered module codomain.
depends_on: Finite convex combinations in convex sets
Finite Jensen inequality.mathlib_notes: Verified in the pinned checkout. For a field with a linear order and strict ordered-ring structure, module domains and codomains, and a partially ordered codomain whose addition and scalar multiplication respect order, ConvexOn.map_sum_le uses an arbitrary finite index set t. It assumes nonnegative weights on t, sum one on t, and membership of all indexed points in the convex domain, then gives the weighted-sum inequality. There is no Fintype, continuity, completeness, separate convex-set, or finite-support hypothesis; weights outside t are unrestricted.

Integral Jensen inequality.description: Jensen's inequality for a continuous real-valued convex function and Bochner integration under a probability measure.
depends_on: Finite convex combinations in convex sets
Integral Jensen inequality.mathlib_notes: Verified in the pinned checkout. ConvexOn.map_integral_le is for a complete real normed space E, a probability measure mu, f : alpha -> E, and a real-valued g : E -> Real. It assumes ConvexOn Real s g, ContinuousOn g s, IsClosed s, almost-everywhere membership f x in s, Integrable f mu, and Integrable (g composed with f) mu. There is no separate sigma-finiteness, measurability, or integral-membership hypothesis; Convex.integral_mem derives that the Bochner integral lies in s. The finite nonzero measure variant is map_average_le and uses normalized averages. MeasureTheory.average_eq_integral is the supporting normalization declaration defined in Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Integral/Average.lean; the recorded mathlib_file is the primary home of the Jensen theorems.

Continuous linear maps.description: Bundled linear or semilinear maps whose underlying functions are continuous.
Continuous linear maps.mathlib_notes: Verified in the pinned checkout. For semirings R and S, a ring homomorphism sigma : R ->+* S, topological additive commutative monoids M and N, and module structures, ContinuousLinearMap bundles a sigma-semilinear map with continuity. The basic structure requires no topology on R or S and no compatibility between scalar multiplication, topology, or addition. The semilinear notation is M ->SL[sigma] N; M ->L[R] N specializes to the identity homomorphism. The listed constructors, coercion lemmas, and continuity projections expose the bundle's exact interface.

Strong dual space.description: The type of continuous scalar-valued linear functionals, without imposing extra topological-algebra compatibility at the definition boundary.
Strong dual space.mathlib_notes: Verified in the pinned checkout. StrongDual R E is the abbreviation E ->L[R] R under Semiring R, TopologicalSpace R, TopologicalSpace E, AddCommMonoid E, and Module R E. Its definition requires no topology-algebra compatibility assumptions. It is distinct from the algebraic dual Module.Dual R E and from WeakDual R E, which equips the same continuous functionals with the weak-star topology.

Operator norm of a continuous linear map.id: Operator norm of a continuous linear map
Operator norm of a continuous linear map.description: Defines the operator norm as the infimum of all nonnegative pointwise norm bounds and installs it as the norm of a continuous semilinear map.
Operator norm of a continuous linear map.mathlib_notes: Verified in the pinned checkout. ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm is a namespace definition, not a structure field or protected definition. For seminormed additive commutative groups over nontrivially normed fields and a ring homomorphism sigma, it is the infimum of nonnegative constants giving a global pointwise norm bound. Neither opNorm, hasOpNorm, nor norm_def requires RingHomIsometric sigma; norm_def identifies the installed norm definitionally with opNorm. Isometry is needed only for downstream existence, least-bound, evaluation, and seminorm-structure results. Norm separation is unnecessary.

Pointwise bound controls the operator no.id: Pointwise bound controls the operator norm
Pointwise bound controls the operator no.description: Converts a nonnegative uniform pointwise linear bound into an operator-norm bound for a continuous semilinear map.
depends_on: Operator norm of a continuous linear map
Pointwise bound controls the operator no.mathlib_notes: Verified in the pinned checkout. ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_le_bound holds for continuous semilinear maps between seminormed additive commutative groups over nontrivially normed fields, with normed-space scalar structures and an arbitrary scalar ring homomorphism. It requires 0 <= M and a pointwise bound norm (f x) <= M * norm x, and concludes norm f <= M. RingHomIsometric is not required; M = 0 and subsingleton spaces are allowed. There is no completeness or norm-separation assumption.

Operator norm controls evaluation.description: Bounds every value of a continuous semilinear map by its operator norm times the input norm.
depends_on: Operator norm of a continuous linear map
Operator norm controls evaluation.mathlib_notes: Verified in the pinned checkout. ContinuousLinearMap.le_opNorm applies to continuous semilinear maps between seminormed additive commutative groups over nontrivially normed fields, with normed-space structures and RingHomIsometric sigma. It states norm (f x) <= norm f * norm x. For ordinary continuous linear maps the identity scalar homomorphism is automatically isometric. No completeness or norm-separation assumption is required. The installed norm is definitionally opNorm; similarly named ContinuousMap and BoundedContinuousFunction results are unrelated.

Inner product as a continuous sesquiline.id: Inner product as a continuous sesquilinear map
Inner product as a continuous sesquiline.description: Bundles the inner product as a continuous conjugate-linear map into the strong dual.
Inner product as a continuous sesquiline.mathlib_notes: Verified in the pinned checkout. For an RCLike field K, a seminormed additive commutative group E, and InnerProductSpace K E, innerSL K has type E ->L*[K] (E ->L[K] K), whose codomain is definitionally StrongDual K E. It sends x and y to inner K x y. The outer map is semilinear over starRingEnd K and hence conjugate-linear, while each inner functional is K-linear. Over Real the star is trivial; over Complex it is genuine. No completeness, finite-dimensionality, or nontriviality assumption on E is required.

Norm of the inner product functional.id: Norm of the inner product functional
Norm of the inner product functional.description: Identifies the operator norm of an inner-product functional with the norm of its representing vector.
depends_on: Inner product as a continuous sesquilinear map
Operator norm of a continuous linear map
Pointwise bound controls the operator norm
Norm of the inner product functional.mathlib_notes: Verified in the pinned checkout. For an RCLike field K, a seminormed additive commutative group E, InnerProductSpace K E, and x : E, innerSL_apply_norm states norm (innerSL K x) = norm x. No CompleteSpace, Nontrivial, or NormedAddCommGroup assumption is required. The argument order is conjugate-linear in x and linear in the functional argument. This is distinct from InnerProductSpace.innerSL_norm, which concerns the whole outer map and has stronger assumptions. Its proof explicitly invokes opNorm_le_bound, le_opNorm, norm_inner_le_norm, and inner_self_eq_norm_sq_to_K, and the graph records those proof dependencies.

Isometric Riesz embedding.description: Embeds a normed inner-product space conjugate-linearly and isometrically into its strong dual.
depends_on: Norm of the inner product functional
Inner product as a continuous sesquilinear map
Isometric Riesz embedding.mathlib_notes: Verified in the pinned checkout. For an RCLike field K, a seminormed additive commutative group E, and InnerProductSpace K E, toDualMap is the conjugate-linear norm-preserving map x |-> (y |-> inner K x y) into StrongDual K E. It is built from innerSL and innerSL_apply_norm. When E is a normed additive commutative group, norm preservation gives injectivity and the usual isometric embedding. No completeness is required; completeness enters only for InnerProductSpace.toDual and its surjectivity. The StrongDual codomain is definitionally E ->L[K] K.

Hilbert projection theorem for complete.id: Hilbert projection theorem for complete convex sets
Hilbert projection theorem for complete.description: Establishes attainment of distance to a nonempty complete convex subset of a real inner-product space.
Hilbert projection theorem for complete.mathlib_notes: Verified in the pinned checkout. For a normed additive commutative group F with InnerProductSpace Real F, the theorem assumes K.Nonempty, IsComplete K, and Convex Real K. For every u it returns v in K satisfying norm (u - v) = iInf over w : K of norm (u - w). No ambient CompleteSpace F is required. Its type asserts existence rather than uniqueness; norm_eq_iInf_iff_real_inner_le_zero supplies the minimizer characterization from which uniqueness can be derived.

Orthogonal projection onto a closed subs.id: Orthogonal projection onto a closed subspace
Orthogonal projection onto a closed subs.description: Constructs subtype- and ambient-valued continuous orthogonal projectors and records membership, orthogonality, uniqueness, and minimality.
depends_on: Minimizer characterizations for convex sets and subspaces
Orthogonal projection onto a closed subs.mathlib_notes: Verified in the pinned checkout under RCLike K, NormedAddCommGroup E, and InnerProductSpace K E. orthogonalProjectionOnto U : E ->L[K] U is subtype-valued, while starProjection U : E ->L[K] E is ambient-valued; bridge lemmas identify their values. Membership, residual orthogonality, uniqueness, and minimality are stated for starProjection, with minimality as an iInf over x : U. The generic construction assumes U.HasOrthogonalProjection. If E is complete and U is closed, U is complete and HasOrthogonalProjection.ofCompleteSpace supplies that instance. eq_starProjection_of_mem_of_inner_eq_zero exposes the self-inner-product uniqueness step. orthogonal_eq_bot_iff, defined in Projection/Submodule.lean, is the projection bridge used by Frechet-Riesz surjectivity. Older orthogonalProjection and orthogonalProjectionFn names are deprecated.

Frechet-Riesz representation theorem.description: Identifies a complete inner-product space conjugate-linearly and isometrically with its strong dual.
depends_on: Orthogonal projection onto a closed subspace
Frechet-Riesz representation theorem.mathlib_notes: Verified in the pinned checkout. For an RCLike field K, NormedAddCommGroup E, InnerProductSpace K E, and CompleteSpace E, InnerProductSpace.toDual K E has type E equivalent conjugate-linearly and isometrically to StrongDual K E. It is built from toDualMap by surjectivity; Mathlib proves surjectivity using orthogonal-projection machinery for the kernel of a functional. toDual_symm_apply identifies the representing vector. Uniqueness and norm equality are generic consequences of equivalence injectivity and norm_map rather than separate named Riesz theorems. No Nontrivial E assumption is required.

Finite convex combinations in convex set.id: Finite convex combinations in convex sets
Finite convex combinations in convex set.description: Centers of mass with nonnegative weights of positive total mass remain in a convex set; consequently finite weighted sums do so when the weights sum to one.
Finite convex combinations in convex set.mathlib_notes: Verified in the pinned checkout. Finset.centerMass is the inverse total weight acting on the weighted finite sum and itself requires only a field, an additive commutative group, and a module. Under a linear order and strict ordered-ring structure, Convex.centerMass_mem assumes nonnegative weights on the explicit Finset, positive total mass, and membership of every indexed point. Convex.sum_mem specializes to total weight one and concludes membership of the raw weighted sum. The index type is arbitrary, values outside the Finset are irrelevant, and no topology, norm, completeness, finite-dimensionality, Fintype, or global finite-support assumption is required.

Self-inner-product and norm definiteness.description: Relates a vector's self-inner-product to its squared norm and, with norm separation, characterizes zero and nonzero vectors.
Self-inner-product and norm definiteness.mathlib_notes: Verified in the pinned checkout. For an RCLike scalar field and a seminormed inner-product space, inner_self_eq_norm_sq_to_K states that the self-inner-product is the square in K of the coerced norm, (norm x : K) ^ 2. The equivalences inner_self_eq_zero and inner_self_ne_zero require NormedAddCommGroup, exactly where norm separation is needed. The norm-functional proof uses the squared-norm identity, orthogonal-projection uniqueness uses the zero equivalence, and Frechet-Riesz surjectivity uses the nonzero equivalence. No completeness or separate Nontrivial assumption is required.

Cauchy-Schwarz inequality for inner prod.description: Bounds the norm of an RCLike inner product by the product of the vector norms.
Cauchy-Schwarz inequality for inner prod.mathlib_notes: Verified in the pinned checkout. Under RCLike scalars, SeminormedAddCommGroup E, and InnerProductSpace K E, norm_inner_le_norm states norm (inner K x y) <= norm x * norm y. It requires neither completeness nor norm separation. Mathlib uses it to construct innerSL as a continuous map and for the upper operator-norm bound in innerSL_apply_norm.

Squared-norm sum and difference expansio.description: Expands squared norms of sums and differences through the real part of the inner product, with specialized real formulas.
Squared-norm sum and difference expansio.mathlib_notes: Verified in the pinned checkout for seminormed RCLike inner-product spaces. norm_add_sq and norm_sub_sq use RCLike.re of inner K x y; norm_add_sq_real and norm_sub_sq_real are the corresponding real-scalar formulas. All four statements use powers ^ 2 and require neither norm separation nor completeness. strongConvexOn_iff_convex uses the real formulas through its auxiliary calculation, while norm_eq_iInf_iff_real_inner_le_zero directly uses norm_sub_sq.

Parallelogram and Pythagorean identities.description: Provides the norm parallelogram law and the Pythagorean norm identity for orthogonal vectors in an RCLike inner-product space.
Parallelogram and Pythagorean identities.mathlib_notes: Verified in the pinned checkout for seminormed RCLike inner-product spaces. parallelogram_law_with_norm_mul takes the scalar K explicitly and states the norm-product form used by the complete-convex minimizer proof. The Pythagorean declaration takes the directed premise inner K x y = 0 and also states products of norms; reverse orthogonality suffices by conjugate symmetry. It is used to bound projection onto a subspace along its orthogonal complement and establish continuity. Neither result requires norm separation or completeness.

Minimizer characterizations for convex s.id: Minimizer characterizations for convex sets and subspaces
Minimizer characterizations for convex s.description: Specializes complete-convex minimizer existence to complete subspaces and characterizes minimizing points by residual orthogonality.
depends_on: Hilbert projection theorem for complete convex sets
Minimizer characterizations for convex s.mathlib_notes: Verified in the pinned checkout. The complete-subspace existence theorem assumes only completeness of the subspace and derives convexity and nonemptiness before applying complete-convex minimizer existence; ambient completeness is unnecessary. The real convex-set theorem characterizes a minimizer by inner Real (u - v) (w - v) <= 0 and uses norm_sub_sq. The real and RCLike submodule variants characterize minimizers by inner K (u - v) w = 0. Only existence needs completeness. HasOrthogonalProjection.ofCompleteSpace uses the existence theorem and RCLike equivalence; starProjection_minimal directly uses the RCLike equivalence.
